title: AI debt collection platform CreditNirvana exposed about 6.6 million accounts and 315,000 call recordings
date_note: Published November 18; the flaws were reported May 30 and fixed June 2, 2026.
summary: Researcher Eaton Zveare reported two flaws in the CreditNirvana collections platform: a hardcoded API key in the AI call centre and a login bypass in the main platform. They exposed about 6.6 million accounts and about 315,000 call recordings. Both were fixed on June 2, 2026. Nothing shows attackers used them.
plain: Two security holes in an AI debt-collection service made millions of borrowers' records and call recordings reachable without a proper login. They were fixed in June.
exec: Shows third-party AI collections platforms can expose lenders' customer data at scale; lenders using them inherit the risk.
action: If you run CreditNirvana, confirm the call centre is on 2.0.0 and the collections platform on 4.8.2, per CERT-In; lenders should review vendor access controls.
impact: About 6.6 million accounts and about 315,000 call recordings accessible; no exploitation shown.

validation.note: Researcher's own write-up and Receivables Info (reporting Wired's findings) agree on numbers, CVEs and the June 2 fix; the vendor did not comment to Wired. Wired itself could not be loaded.

review.note: 6.6M accounts, 315k recordings, two flaws, 30 May report, 2 June fix, CVEs, versions and no-exploitation wording against researcher write-up and Receivables Info; Wired not read
